findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Scope line range from `runner.py:507-581` to `runner.py:555-629` (the actual except spine: first `except UsageLimitExceeded` through `raise provider_err from exc`).
evidence: runner.py:507 is `_call_label = (` — the observability label, inside the run() body but BEFORE the try/except block
runner.py:555 is the first `except UsageLimitExceeded as exc:` — the real start of the except spine
runner.py:629 is `raise provider_err from exc` — the last statement of the last except arm
The plan's stated range 507-581 misses lines 582-629 entirely, including the broad Exception arm's sampling-parameter reclassification and disposition attachment
findings.finding: The Scope section states the except spine occupies 'runner.py:507-581', but the actual except arms begin at line 555 (first `except UsageLimitExceeded`) and end at line 629 (last `raise provider_err from exc`). Line 507 is the observability label setup (_call_label), which is pre-try-block scaffolding, not part of the except spine.
scenarios: An implementer following the stated line range will miss ~48 lines of the broad except arm (lines 582-629), including the disposition classifier attachment and the classify_llm_failure call that AC line 3 depends on.
A reviewer auditing the commit diff against '507-581' will believe coverage is complete when nearly half the broad arm is outside the stated range.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Scope bullet to: `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:555-629 -> interpret_failure(...)` with explicit parameters (exc, run_messages, req_limit, eff_max_iter, _call_label, req, ran_model, _t0).

evidence: AC1 and AC2 both open with 'a test asserts...', establishing an explicit proving pattern
AC3 uses passive declarative voice with no 'a test asserts' prefix and no described assertion
Under E6 taxonomy item (a): 'every completion-relevant claim has a concrete proving command/check'
findings.finding: AC3 ('the classified disposition is still attached as METADATA without changing the raised type') does not specify a test assertion or proving command — unlike AC1 and AC2 which each say 'a test asserts'. It is stated as an invariant to preserve but leaves the executor without a specified verification artifact.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC3: 'the classified disposition is still attached as METADATA without changing the raised type'
scenarios: An executor considers AC3 satisfied by code inspection alone, leaving the metadata-attachment property untested and regressable

With: 'a test asserts that the exception raised by interpret_failure() carries the classified disposition as metadata (e.g. err.disposition is set) while the raised type matches the input exception type — verifiable by inspecting the caught exception in the test body.'

findings.finding: test_llm_failure_matrix.py contains 15+ `CURRENT(runner.py:NNN)` marker strings with hardcoded line numbers (e.g. `runner.py:346`, `runner.py:365`, `runner.py:390`) that pin the exact seam locations of the except arms. After interpret_failure() is extracted, those line numbers will shift in runner.py and the arm bodies will move to a new file/function, making every one of these markers stale. AC5 only requires repointing monkeypatch targets, not these documentation markers. Silently stale markers defeat the 'seam pinning' contract this matrix test was built to enforce.
scenarios: An implementer extracts the except arms and updates monkeypatch targets per AC5, but leaves the CURRENT(runner.py:NNN) strings unchanged; they now point to wrong lines or a seam that no longer exists in runner.py, silently invalidating the seam-pinning documentation for future epic stories.
A future story author reads 'CURRENT(runner.py:365)' expecting to find the broad except arm at that line, finds unrelated code instead, and mis-identifies the seam.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen AC4 to restate the parent's per-commit threshold: 'runner.py's before/after LOC is recorded in the commit message AND the post-extraction count is under 700 (measured on this commit's own diff, not inherited from a sibling)'.
evidence: Leaf AC4: 'runner.py's before/after LOC is recorded in the commit message'
Parent 7f86 AC3: 'EVERY child's commit, AS STACKED IN THE ORDER ABOVE, leaves runner.py under 700 — measured locally on that child's own commit before push and RECORDED in its commit message'
Parent body: 'EVERY CHANGE MUST CLEAR THE 700 GUARD ON ITS OWN (measured; corrects the arithmetic below)'
Parent notes the pure extraction lands at 718 (over 700), requiring comment tightening to reach 699 — so the threshold is the operative constraint, not just the recording
findings.finding: Leaf AC4 records only 'runner.py's before/after LOC' without restating the parent's mandatory under-700 threshold. Parent AC3 (story 7f86) is explicit: 'EVERY child's commit, AS STACKED IN THE ORDER ABOVE, leaves runner.py under 700 — measured locally on that child's own commit before push.' An implementer reading only the leaf's AC4 could log '782 → 718' (the pure-extraction result the parent itself describes) and consider the criterion met, while actually failing the CI gate that blocks the whole relation chain.
scenarios: Implementer extracts the except spine cleanly, records '782 → 718' in the commit message, marks AC4 satisfied — but 718 > 700 means CI casts Verified -1 and wedges the entire relation chain (e6bd, 8229, and everything above).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC4 with: 'runner.py's before/after LOC is recorded in the commit message; the post-extraction LOC must be under 700, measured on this commit alone (comment tightening in run() is permitted per the parent's rule — no measured number, file:line citation, bug/story/epic id, named failure mode, or stated invariant may be dropped).'
